title: Struct-as-Wire-Format / Memory Layout Serialization (STRUCT_LAYOUT_SERIALIZATION)
pattern: Serializing or deserializing data by transmuting or casting a raw byte buffer directly into/from a memory structure without decoding individual fields.
why_bad: Memory layout of `repr(Rust)` is completely non-deterministic and can change across compiler versions. Even under `repr(C)`, compiler-inserted padding is architecture-dependent. It couples the wire format to CPU byte alignment, pointer size, and endianness (Big-endian vs. Little-endian), resulting in severe portability bugs, memory corruption, and undefined behavior.
detection: Look for direct casts from a slice of bytes (`*const u8`) to a reference/pointer of a struct type, or usage of `mem::transmute` across boundary layers (network, disk, or FFI).
fix: Decode fields explicitly from bytes using byte-order-aware routines (e.g., `from_be_bytes()`) or adopt a schema-driven serialization framework (e.g., Protocol Buffers, serde).
source: *Jon Gjengset - Rust For Rustaceans (2021)*, Chapter 3; *Alex Petrov - Database Internals (2019)*, Chapter 3 (Footnote 2); *Benjamin C. Pierce - Types and Programming Languages (2002)*, Chapter 1.
